newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends down on weather, Dec hits 2-yr low.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends down on weather, Dec hits 2-yr low.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on good crop weather, a collapse in wheat futures and bearish export news as new crop December hit a two-year low and threatened to break below its contract low, traders said.
"Some of it came out of the wheat decline and the weather was bearish," said Joe Victor, analyst for Allendale Inc.
The session low for December was $2.51-1/2 a bushel, the lowest level in two years and was near the contract low of $2.49-3/4 set on May 15, 1995.
A contract low of $2.53-1/2 was set in the September, below the previous low of $2.55 set on January 9.
The neighboring wheat pit was pounded by crop-enhancing rainfall over the weekend in the U.S. Great Plains.
Corn belt weather was perceived as conducive to early crop germination and development as widespread weekend rains fell across the Midwest, sources said.
CBOT corn futures closed unchanged to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 6-1/4 at $2.64-1/4 a bushel. New crop December closed 4-1/2 cents lower at $2.52.
New crop was further hit by expectations that USDA's weekly crop progress report, due after the close of trading Tuesday, would show the crop was 97 to 99 percent seeded.
Floor sources continued to compare this year's crop and the record harvest of 1994.
In both years, plantings were completed early and summer weather patterns were cool and wet, traders said.

Old crop contracts struggled with USDA's weekly export inspections data that showed 21,605,000 bushels of corn were inspected for export in the week ended May 22, below trade expectations for 23 million to 29 million bushels.
Fund selling totaled at least 16.0 million bushels, traders said.

Smith Barney sold three million bushels of December as did Dean Witter, traders said. Smith Barney also sold two million bushels of July and E.D. and F. Man International sold two million bushels of July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 60,000 contracts, above the 50,684 traded Friday.

In spread dealings, Tenco Inc did 2.7 million bushels of July/December at 13-1/4 cents, premium July and FIMAT Futures did two million July/December at 12-1/2 cents, premium July. Tenco Inc did two million December/July at 12-3/4 to 13 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 25,482 traded Friday.
